subject: basic-computing
title: Digital Storage
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Name any two cloud storage services.
questions.answer: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive (any two).

questions.q: Write the full form of SSD.
questions.answer: Secondary Storage Device (as used in the textbook).

questions.q: Write the full form of NAS.
questions.answer: Network Attached Storage.

questions.q: Which of these is an optical storage device: hard disk, tape, Blu-ray disk, punch card?
questions.answer: Blu-ray disk.

questions.q: What is online storage?
questions.answer: Storage that is currently connected to the computer.

questions.q: What is offline storage?
questions.answer: Any storage that is not currently connected to the computer.

questions.q: What is the default place where data is stored on a computer?
questions.answer: The hard drive (secondary storage).

questions.q: Name the online storage that needs internet connectivity.
questions.answer: Cloud storage.

questions.q: Which storage was used in earlier times through punching machines?
questions.answer: Punch cards.

questions.q: State true or false: Secondary memory is temporary storage.
questions.answer: False; secondary memory is permanent storage.

questions.q: Which memory in the hierarchy is the fastest?
questions.answer: Register (processor) memory.

questions.q: Where do you see files shared by others in Google Drive?
questions.answer: In the 'Shared with me' section.

questions.q: What is the purpose of data backup in cloud storage?
questions.answer: To keep copies of files so they can be recovered if deleted or corrupted.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is a Hard disk? Explain its structure and working process.
questions.answer: A hard disk is the most common secondary storage device. It has many disks stacked on a cylindrical spindle; data is stored magnetically in concentric tracks; read/write heads on an arm move across the disks to read or write data.

questions.q: How can you broadly categorize the digital storage in terms of Memory Hierarchy?
questions.answer: Internal memory (registers and cache), main memory (RAM), on-line mass storage (secondary storage) and off-line bulk storage (tertiary and offline storage).

questions.q: Describe any 4 core characteristics of storage device technologies on the basis of which they are differentiated.
questions.answer: Volatility (data kept after power off), mutability (read, write, overwrite), accessibility (random or sequential), capacity, performance, security and energy use (any four).

questions.q: Write the steps to create a personal workspace to store, organise and share files using Google Drive.
questions.answer: Step 1: Go to drive.google.com and log in with the Google account. Step 2: Upload files or create files/folders by right-clicking a blank area. Step 3: Right-click the file, choose Share, enter e-mail IDs and set the permission (view, edit, comment).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Tertiary storage devices provide large capacity at low cost. (ii) Blu-ray disc is an optical storage device. (iii) Primary storage stores data permanently. (iv) RAM is tertiary memory.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – primary storage is temporary. (iv) False – RAM is primary (main) memory.

questions.q: Define cloud storage. Write any two benefits of using cloud storage.
questions.answer: Cloud storage is online storage on the web that needs internet. Benefits: files can be accessed anytime and anywhere; it works as a backup; it allows sharing and collaboration; it saves hardware cost (any two).

questions.q: Define digital storage.
questions.answer: The process of storing data electronically on a storage medium in devices such as computers and smartphones.

questions.q: Differentiate between online and offline storage.
questions.answer: Online storage is currently connected to the computer (e.g. hard disk); offline storage is not connected (e.g. a CD kept on a shelf or a tape).

questions.q: Name any two large size, large capacity digital storage devices that are affordable.
questions.answer: Hard drives and magnetic tapes.

questions.q: Write advantages of cloud storage (any four).
questions.answer: Anytime anywhere access, backup and recovery, security with login, cost saving, easy sharing and collaboration.

questions.q: Explain the importance of the collaboration feature of cloud storage with an example.
questions.answer: Many people can work on a document at the same time from different places; for example, classmates can edit a Google Docs project together over the internet.

questions.q: Match: (i) RAM (ii) Tape backup (iii) Flash memory with (a) small size, large capacity (b) medium size, medium capacity (c) large size, very large capacity.

sections.title: Answer the questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the features (characteristics) of a digital storage.
questions.answer: Volatility, mutability, accessibility, addressability, capacity, performance, security and energy use are used to compare storage technologies in the hierarchy.

questions.q: Explain the benefits of cloud storage.
questions.answer: Usability and accessibility; recovery as backup; security through login; cost saving; easy sharing with permissions; automatic data backup; and collaboration by multiple users in real time.

questions.q: Explain the storage hierarchy from register to magnetic tape.
questions.answer: Registers and cache are small, very fast and very expensive; RAM is medium and fast; flash/USB is large and cheap but slower; hard drives have very large capacity and are slow; magnetic tapes are very large, very slow and affordable.

questions.q: Write the steps to use Google Drive to upload, share and organize files.
questions.answer: Go to drive.google.com; upload a file or create files by right-clicking in a white space; right-click the file, choose Share, add e-mail IDs and permissions; use Shared with me to see others' files.

questions.q: Describe the types of digital storage devices used from earlier times till now.
questions.answer: Punch cards; magnetic storage (tapes, floppy disk, hard disk); optical storage (CD, DVD, Blu-ray); USB flash drives; and network storage (NAS, cloud).

questions.q: Explain how cloud storage helps in the case of a system failure, with an example.
questions.answer: A user who saves files on cloud storage can log in from another system and access them anytime, so work is not lost; e.g. an office assistant whose computer fails can still share the document.
